name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=input). No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix equal to its own/any data address). Correctly reflects the datum: it is byte 1 (AH) of the shared union REGS at 0x53A8D, carrying both the INT 16h AH 'input mode' preset (0x10, AH=10h read-enhanced-keyboard) written before the call and the returned scancode read back after. Confirmed by disasm of fd2_wait_for_input_v2 @0x12dac: MOV byte[0x53a8e],0x10; int386(0x16,&regs@0x53a8d,...); MOVZX EAX,byte[0x53a8e]; remap E0/0x52->0x1C, 0x53->0x01.
purpose: AH byte of the shared INT 16h union REGS scratch: holds the AH 'input mode' function preset (0x10 before the call) and the returned keyboard scancode after int386(0x16,...).
logic_summary: Not a standalone global. globals.h defines it as a macro `#define data_fd2_input_key_input_mode (data_fd2_input_int16_regs.h.ah)` over the shared `union REGS data_fd2_input_int16_regs` (storage defined in life/main.c @0x53A8D). Every input-wait routine writes 0x10 here (INT 16h AH=10h read-enhanced-keyboard preset), calls int386(0x16, &data_fd2_input_last_key_pressed, ...) which reads/writes the whole REGS, then reads the AH scancode back from this byte and remaps special scancodes (0xE0 / 'R' 0x52 -> 0x1C Enter; 'S' 0x53 -> 0x01 Esc; some callers also fold ASCII space 0x20 -> Enter). Sharing the union (vs two independent uint8 globals) is mandatory: int386 writes the AH result at last_key+1, and splitting would let the linker separate the bytes and place an unrelated global at byte 1 (clobbering it = dead SFX while the scancode lands in the wrong byte = dead keyboard).
datatype: uint8 (AH member of union REGS at 0x53A8D; accessed as a single byte at every site: MOV byte ptr / MOVZX byte ptr)
element_semantics: On write before int386: INT 16h AH function number (0x10 = read enhanced keyboard). On read after int386: keyboard scancode (post-remap: extended-prefix E0 and Down 0x52 -> Enter 0x1C; Delete 0x53 -> Esc 0x01).
notes: 0x53A8E is byte 1 (AH) of union REGS data_fd2_input_int16_regs @0x53A8D (storage + data-definition comment in life/main.c lines 1056-1063; macro + rationale in globals.h lines 539-551; explanatory note in input.c lines 733-742). All three src locations are mutually consistent and match the disassembly. Ghidra plate lives on the union base 0x53A8D and already states 'byte 1 (0x53A8E, AH) = scancode / INT 16h function number (0x10 preset before read)' plus the macro mapping -- accurate and not stale, so plate left untouched (member byte 0x53A8E has no own plate, by convention the union-base plate documents both members). No src edit was needed (comment already precise). No logic/equivalence issues found. Read as a single byte everywhere (no sign/zero-extension surprises: MOVZX on read, immediate byte store on write).
